description: "The process of converting text or other input into discrete units that a model can process."
term: "Tokenization"

## Simple explanation

Tokenization breaks input into units a model can process. For language
models, those units are often words, word pieces, punctuation, or special
markers, each mapped to an ID.

## Technical explanation

A tokenizer applies a vocabulary and segmentation algorithm to map strings
to token IDs. Common subword schemes include byte-pair encoding, WordPiece,
and unigram language models. Normalization, unknown-token behavior, and
special-token handling vary by tokenizer.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Tokenization determines sequence length and influences what patterns a
model can represent. It affects context limits, cost, multilingual
coverage, code handling, and compatibility between training and inference.

## How it works

Text is normalized according to the tokenizer's rules, segmented into
vocabulary units, and converted into integer IDs. The model consumes those
IDs; generated IDs are mapped back to text during decoding.

## Practical example

Before deploying a model on multilingual inputs, an engineer can inspect
token counts for representative languages and scripts. A tokenizer that
uses many tokens for some languages may increase latency and reduce the
effective amount of text that fits in the context.

## Common misconceptions

- Tokenization is not always splitting on spaces; subword and byte-level
  schemes can divide words in surprising ways.
- A model and its tokenizer are a matched pair; substituting another
  tokenizer changes the meaning of token IDs.
